transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20
Time: 14:00 EST
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jared (Redwood AE), Sasha (Redwood SE), Maya (Cascade Head of Search), Liam (Cascade Infra), Priya (Cascade Data Scientist)

[00:00] Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we're gonna go through a quick discovery — try to understand your search stack and what you're looking to do with embeddings and reranking.
[00:18] Maya: Thanks Jared, appreciate it. We'll give a quick context — Cascade has about 12 million medical documents, we index for provider search and patient Q&A. Current infra is ElasticSearch + a separate vector DB for embeddings, it's kinda hybrid.
[00:33] Liam: yeah, we run ES on-prem for PHI zones and then a managed vector DB in cloud for the rest. We're looking at options to improve reranking quality particularly for long queries and clinical synonyms.
[00:48] Sasha: got it. are you currently doing reranking by sending top-k from ES then reranking with an embedding model? what's the flow?
[00:56] Priya: Exactly. ES for recall (BM25), then an embedding model for rerank. We precompute doc vectors at 1536 dims, and online queries we embed at 1536, cosine sim, then a small cross-encoder for final scoring — that cross-encoder is expensive.
[01:14] Jared: Right, so the common pattern. Quick qual: what's your QPS and latency targets for user-facing search?
[01:20] Maya: Peak 300 QPS across our primary region, p95 latency target for search is 200-250ms. Rerank budget is ~50ms ideally, but we can tolerate 100ms for better relevance.
[01:36] Liam: also important we keep PHI inside our VPC; any hosted option needs VPC peering or Private deployment. SOC2 and KMS integration are must-haves.
[01:45] Sasha: understood. On the infra side, are you happiest using dedicated capacity vs host? any preference?
[01:51] Maya: We're evaluating. Hosted is attractive for dev and ops simplicity but dedicated or private might be required for compliance and predictable throughput.
[02:04] Sasha: Cool. A couple of threads we'll hit today: model choice for embedding dimensionality (768 vs 1536 vs 4096), vector DB integration patterns (native Redwood embeddings + vector store vs using existing DB like Pinecone), throughput/benchmarking and hybrid search configs (how many recall docs to send to embedding stage).
[02:22] Priya: On dimensionality, we've been using 1536 from an off-the-shelf model and it's been fine, but curious if going to 768 with fine-tuning or 4096 for specialty clinical tokens would help. Also cost per embedding is a concern at our QPS.
[02:38] Sasha: Right — tradeoffs: smaller dim lowers storage and embedding compute; larger dims may help capture clinical nuance but adds vector DB storage and search cost. Redwood can host multiple embedding model variants; we can recommend a quantized 1536 or a tuned 768 for similar quality with lower perf cost depending on evals.
[02:54] Maya: And for reranking, can Redwood host the cross-encoder? or do we need to run that ourselves?
[03:00] Jared: We can run cross-encoders in Dedicated or Private deployments; Hosted can run smaller cross-encoders but heavy cross-encoders at scale usually go on Dedicated for predictable latency. We can also do a two-stage approach — embed + dense rerank on vector scores, and only run cross-encoder for top 5.
[03:18] Liam: top-5 cross-encoder approach seems right but we need throughput capacity planning — if we have 300 QPS and we send top-20 recall to embeddings and then cross-encoder on top-5, that's 1500 embed ops/sec plus cross-encoder compute. Do you have guidance on batching and how Redwood handles continuous batching?
[03:38] Sasha: yes. Redwood runtime supports continuous batching and dynamic batching policies. For embeddings we can batch across requests to amortize model cost; Dedicated gives more control over batch sizes and max latency. For your p95 250ms target, we can configure batching cutoffs and a throughput-optimized pool. Also prefix/KV cache is more relevant for generation workloads, but we do have caching for cold doc vectors during re-ingestion pipelines.
[04:05] Priya: What's the typical latency for a 1536 embedding on Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated?
[04:11] Sasha: Hosted: p50 ~12-18ms per embed in our public benchmarks for a 1536 model; p95 can be higher depending on tenancy. Dedicated: you get pinned GPUs, so p95 can be ~20-30ms for higher throughput depending on batch. Cross-encoder latencies vary hugely — small cross-encoders (60-120ms) vs large (300ms+).
[04:34] Maya: We care about vector DB integration — we currently push vectors to Pinecone. Would Redwood replace that or integrate with it?
[04:42] Jared: both models supported. Many customers prefer using their existing vector DB and ask Redwood to produce embeddings via API and push to the vector store. We also have an opinionated integration path where Redwood can host the embeddings and provide a search endpoint that does vector search + rerank inside Redwood runtime; that reduces network hops but requires more due-diligence for PHI.
[05:03] Priya: If we keep our Pinecone cluster, can Redwood call Pinecone directly inside a pipeline to retrieve candidates? Latency adds though.
[05:10] Sasha: Yes, that's common. We recommend running the first-stage vector search in the same region and minimize cross-network hops. For tight latency budgets, Dedicated with co-located vector DB or Private deployment with on-prem vector DB gives best p95.
[05:26] Liam: about dimensionality — our storage cost for 12M docs at 1536 dims is non-trivial. Any recommendations for compression or quantization?
[05:34] Sasha: On vector DB side, many vector stores support product quantization (PQ) or 8-bit/4-bit encodings. For embedding models we recommend evaluating quantized embeddings or L2-normalized lower-dim variants. Redwood Optimize can run experiments and recommend quantization profiles and model variants per workload.
[05:52] Maya: Security questions: SOC2, audit logs, SSO, KMS — how are those handled for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
[06:01] Jared: Hosted: we provide SOC2 attestation and tenant isolation, but for PHI some customers require VPC peering and dedicated networking; Dedicated: reserved GPU pools with customer network controls and enterprise KMS integration; Private: customer-managed control plane and full on-prem options. We'll share our security whitepaper and SOC2 report.
[06:19] Liam: KMS: can we bring our own key to encrypt model artifacts and embeddings?
[06:24] Sasha: Yes — Dedicated and Private support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). Hosted can integrate with cloud KMS for some enterprise tiers, but BYOK is typically in Dedicated/Private.
[06:36] Priya: For the benchmark, what data should we provide and what's the expected deliverable?
[06:41] Sasha: We usually ask for a sample of representative documents (anonymized), a query set annotated with relevance judgments (or at least expected positives), and target QPS/latency. We can run 500k-vector indexing and run hybrid search throughput tests and produce a report — precision/recall, latency percentiles, cost estimate for Hosted vs Dedicated.
[07:01] Maya: timeline?
[07:03] Jared: We can send pricing and security docs this week. For a benchmark we'd aim to start in early Jan once we have the sample dataset — 1-2 weeks to run and analyze.
[07:13] Priya: For hybrid search — are you recommending BM25 + vector or purely vector?
[07:18] Sasha: Hybrid is common for you; BM25 for recall and vector rerank captures lexical signals. Another option is a single-stage dense retrieval model but that requires retraining and heavy QA. For practical purposes, BM25 + embed rerank (and optionally cross-encoder top-k) is low-risk.
[07:35] Liam: anything about model versioning and rollouts? We need ability to revert and A/B test embedding models and reranker configs.
[07:42] Jared: Redwood Console supports model pinning, canary rollouts, and metrics per-model. Redwood Optimize can run comparisons on eval sets to detect regressions. We'll include docs on rollout policies.
[07:56] Maya: cost question — do you have a sample cost estimate for 300 QPS and 12M vectors for Hosted vs Dedicated?
[08:04] Jared: We'll run a back-of-envelope in the pricing doc; generally Dedicated amortizes cost better at that scale but has commit requirements. Hosted is higher per-unit but less ops overhead. We'll include multiple scenarios in the sheet.
[08:18] Priya: Any limits on embedding dimensionality or storage?
[08:22] Sasha: No hard limits, but vector stores and search latencies vary with dim. We'll recommend experiments: 768 quantized, 1536 baseline, perhaps 2048 if we see gains in relevance. Redwood can host those variants; Optimize will recommend per-eval results.
[08:38] Maya: Are there common gotchas moving from hosted to private?
[08:42] Jared: Main ones: networking (VPC routes, egress), KMS setup and key rotation policies, compliance stamping, and on-prem GPU procurement. We have a Private runbook we share.
[08:56] Liam: Regarding the cross-encoder compute — do you have guidance on batching or sharding that work?
[09:01] Sasha: Yes. For cross-encoders it's common to batch multiple candidate pairs; Dedicated allows fixed GPU pools for low jitter. We can set autoscaling policies for bursts, but must model cost for steady-state vs bursts.
[09:15] Maya: Ok this is super helpful. Quick recap and next steps?
[09:20] Jared: Recap: we'll send pricing and security docs this week, Sasha will prepare a benchmark plan and sample script for the 500k vectors, you (Maya/Priya) will share anonymized sample docs + query set, and we'll schedule a technical deep dive with Liam's infra team in early Jan.
[09:40] Priya: Sounds good. Also would like an estimate on storage cost and guidance on PQ settings before we start.
[09:47] Sasha: We'll include PQ and quantization recommendations in the benchmark plan.
[09:52] Jared: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with docs and calendar invites.
[09:59] Maya: Thanks, talk soon.

Action recap in call: send pricing & sec docs, prepare benchmark, share sample data, schedule deep dive.

(Transcript end)
